column2: Grand Crusader

Twice now [Root.GetTitledFirstName] has ridden at the head of a Great Crusade, and twice the banners of the faith have followed [Root.GetHerHim] to victory. Across all the lands of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] faiths [Root.GetSheHe] is hailed as the most fearless of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faithful, and peasants press forward to touch the hem of [Root.GetHerHis] cloak as [Root.GetSheHe] passes.\n\nThe minstrels already sing of the [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] line as the sword of the gods. Whatever crusades are called in the years to come, the children of this house will be expected to ride in the van.
Where the gods lead, I follow.
Commander of the Crusade

Forward! I roar, cutting down another man who charges me. "For [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]! To victory!"

The press of the battle carries my guards away, and I set my teeth for what comes next. Through the dust I can see their commander, sitting his horse well behind the line with a grin on his face. If I fall today, he falls with me. Cut follows cut, and his grin fades to a grimace as the fight he thought was far away drags him in.

When the battle settles, I stand over him and what is left of his retinue. "My [Root.GetLordLady], are you hurt?" one of my guards gasps, staring at the blood on me. Little of it is mine.
Hurt? I have never felt better.
The Errantry War

[From.GetTitledName] has declared an Errantry War against the Sultans of Araby. The knights of Antoch have long kept their watch on the edge of the sands, and now they mean to carry the Lady's banner into the desert itself, as the knights of Bretonnia did when the Arabyans first dared to land in Estalia.

Every Knight Errant who rides south and lives may come home a Knight of the Realm, and the young lords of Bretonnia are already sharpening their lances. In the desert cities the sorcerers of the Sultans are said to be calling up winds and djinn to meet them.

It will be years before the host is ready to sail. When it does, the sand will drink a great deal of blood.
For the Lady and the King!
Perhaps I could ask the §Y[d_knights_of_antoch.GetName]§! to march on my Arabyan neighbours?
The Bretonnians and their endless questing.
Let them bleed each other in the sand.
Let them come. The desert is a grave for armies.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName]

[northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName] is a danger to every faithful soul in the south, and I agree that [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetSheHe] must be dealt with. My knights are ready to ride for the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands. I ask nothing of you but your prayers, and that you keep vigil for us in the chapel of the Lady.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
Ride, and may the Lady guard you.
Wait. I must think on this.

[Root.GetTitledName]

My knights are ready to march against [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName], but horses, ships and men-at-arms do not come cheap, and the desert eats all three. If you want this war, you must help pay for it.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
Take the gold, and ride.
Wait. I must think on this.

[Root.GetTitledName]

I agree that [northern_crusade_potential_target.GetTitledName] is a dangerous foe, but my order cannot wage war on the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands from across the sea. Give us a foothold close to the enemy, a castle and the land around it, and my knights will do the rest.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
The land is yours. Ride.
Give §Y[From.GetTitledName]§! all the land of your realm in §Y[northern_crusade_duchy_title.GetFullBaseName]§!
Wait. I must think on this.
The Knights Sail South

The host of Antoch has sailed for the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands, a forest of lances and pennants on the decks, the Grail embroidered on every sail. The knights sing hymns to the Lady as they go, and the Knights Errant among them talk of nothing but the glory waiting in the sand.

Their first quarry is [northern_crusade_target_character.GetTitledFirstName], lord of [northern_crusade_target_character.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName]. If [northern_crusade_target_character.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName] falls, the order means to make it a fortress from which to bring the rest of the [northern_crusade_kingdom_title.GetAdjective] lands to heel.

No quarter has been promised to the servants of the Sultans.
For the Lady and the King!
The Bretonnians and their endless questing.
And so the knights ride into the sand...

To the esteemed [Root.GetTitledName]

The Knights of Antoch thank you for your aid in the war for [northern_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. Your name will be read out in our chapel at every vigil.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the esteemed [Root.GetTitledName]

The Knights of Antoch thank you for your aid in the war for [northern_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. Your name will be read out in our chapel at every vigil, and we send with this letter a share of the spoils of the desert, as is only right.

In the Lady's name,
[From.GetTitledName]
It was the least I could do.
The Errantry War Fails

Twice the Knights of Antoch have ridden into the desert, and twice the sand has thrown them back. Thirst, sickness and the sorcery of the Sultans have done what no Arabyan lance could, and [From.GetTitledName] has called the Errantry War to an end.

The knights limp home with empty saddles behind them, and the Knights Errant who rode south hoping for glory have found graves instead. In the courts of Araby the Sultans are already talking of the north, and of how soft the faithful of the Lady have grown.

Bretonnia's southern shore may soon see dhows full of raiders.
How could the Lady abandon us?
Another failure for the [From.Religion.GetName] faithful.
Neither side deserved to win.
The desert has spoken!
Friend of Antoch

A great honour guard of the Knights of Antoch has ridden up to the gates of [Root.Capital.GetName], with [From.GetTitledName] [From.GetHerselfHimself] at their head. In thanks for my aid in their wars against Araby, the order has named me and all my blood the friends of Antoch, and [From.GetTitledName] presents me with a knight's helm bearing the order's crest.\n\nFor as long as my line endures, the order will ride at our side should we ever have need of them.
It is an honour.
[northern_crusade_kingdom.GetBaseName] Is Won

It has been a long and bitter war between the Knights of Antoch and the people of the [northern_crusade_kingdom.GetAdjective] lands, but the Errantry War has at last ended in victory for the Lady.

The chapels of the Grail now stand where the domes of Araby once rose, and the knights of the order ride the desert roads to keep them safe for the faithful. A score of Knights Errant have come home as Knights of the Realm, and the minstrels have a new war to sing about.

The Sultans of Araby will not soon forget it.
For the Lady and the King!
Well fought, I suppose.
Bretonnia grows bold.
The sand will take it back, in time.

Antochian Blood of [Root.GetFirstName]
For [Root.GetHerHis] aid to the Knights of Antoch in their wars against Araby, [Root.GetHerHis] line is held a sworn friend of the order.
Helm of Antoch
Every §YKnight Errant§! who rode in the Errantry War becomes a §YKnight of the Realm§!
A knight's helm crested with the Grail and the arms of the Knights of Antoch, given only to the order's truest friends.

The fleet rides at anchor off [diverted_creditor.Capital.GetName]: galleys, cogs and horse-ships enough to carry the whole Errantry War to the sands of Araby. [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] built every hull of it on the order's word, and now the reckoning has come. The coffers of the order hold not a tenth of the price.\n\nThe Tilean does not shout. A map is unrolled across the table instead. "[diverted_port.GetName] lies on your road south, my lord. Its walls are old, its granaries are full, and its master, [diverted_target.GetTitledName], has cost me more than ships ever will. Take it for me, keep the plunder, and we shall call the debt paid. The Lady need never know."
[diverted_port.GetName] it is. The Lady forgives a debt honourably paid.
Empty the coffers. We pay in gold, not in Old World blood.
A knight of the Grail owes nothing to a merchant. Let him whistle for his coin.
The Errantry Turns

Word runs along the coasts of Tilea faster than any galley. The fleet built to carry [From.GetTitledName] and the Knights of Antoch to Araby has not sailed south. It has turned for [diverted_port.GetName], and the knights mean to storm it at the bidding of [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName], who built their ships and was never paid for them.\n\nIn the temples of Myrmidia the priests are bricking up the treasuries, and [diverted_target.GetTitledName] is calling every sellsword in Tilea to the walls.
Treachery! Every sellsword in Tilea, to the walls!
A debt is a debt, and now it will be paid in [diverted_target.GetFirstName]'s gold.
The Lady weeps to see her knights turned hired swords.
So much for the honour of Bretonnia.
The Sack of [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName]

[diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] has fallen. For three days the knights of the Errantry War and the sellswords of [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] went through the city street by street. They stripped the gold from the altars of Myrmidia, dragged the strongboxes of the merchant princes down to the quays and burned whatever they could not carry. Those who fought were cut down in the canals and piazzas, and those who did not were robbed all the same.\n\nWhat is left of the city now belongs to [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName]. The knights have the gold, and the fleet sails on for Araby with blood on its banners.
The Lady's work needs gold. Let none ask how it was got.
The debt is paid, and [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] is mine.
They will pay for this, every knight of them.
Knights of the Grail, sacking Old World cities like Norscan reavers!
The Errantry War has found easier prey than Araby.
Your house founds the bloodline §YBlood of the Sack§!
The Siege of [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName] Is Broken

The knights of the Errantry War have been thrown back from [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName]. Tilean crossbows and pikes held the walls, and the fleet built to carry the knights to Araby now carries their wounded home. [diverted_creditor.GetTitledName] has neither the city nor the coin, and the Knights of Antoch have neither the city nor their honour.
The Lady has judged us. We sail for Araby, and pray.
Let every knight of Bretonnia remember [diverted_port_title.GetBaseName].
Sellswords would have done better, and cost less.

Sacked by the Errantry
Knights of the Grail plundered this city to pay for their fleet. Its trade is ruined, its granaries are empty and its people are still clearing the rubble.
Blood of the Sack
The house of the knight who turned the Errantry War on a Tilean port and paid the debt of ships in Old World blood. Its heirs are feared, and they know how to make a prisoner talk.

Once a game, the Tilean prince who built the fleet of the Errantry War may demand his price, and the Knights of Antoch may sack Miragliano, Remas or Luccini to pay it.
The Knights of Antoch always sail straight for Araby.
